newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Breather beckons for Belgian bonds.
newsitem.headline: Breather beckons for Belgian bonds.

text.p: The Belgian OLO market is likely to have an untroubled week due to a more relaxed attitude on U.S. and German bond markets, analysts said on Monday.
"It looks like we've entered a stabilisation phase," said Koen Dierckx at Kredietbank.

Strong initial Q3 data in the U.S. had been tempered by good inflation figures. "The bond market is a bit more relaxed now," he said. The negative impact of uncertainty over the Bundesbank's near-term policy had also waned.
At 1442 GMT the benchmark 2007 OLO yielded 5.73 percent, down from 5.75 on Thursday. The market was closed on Friday.
Dierckx said the drop of the dollar had stripped the Bundesbank of the direct cause for a rate rise.
He noted that there were few important U.S. data on this week's calendar and that little of note was expected from the meeting of the U.S. policy making Federal Open Market Committee on Tuesday.
But the market was unlikely to see an influx of capital from investors moving out of stocks following stock market weakness in recent sessions.
"That money would be placed in the short end, not in OLOs," Dierckx said.
One analyst said they expected more steepening in the yield curve, after it had remained relatively flat in recent weeks, once the Bundesbank would start using its "interest rate weapon".
